title.en: Perimeter: the border of a shape

text.en: Preetha and Adrit's grandmother made a quilt from old clothes. She wants to decorate its border with lace. Which lace length will cover the entire border - 40 units, 50 units or 25 units?

The length of the border of a shape is called its perimeter. The lace must be exactly as long as the perimeter.
The perimeter of a rectangle is length + breadth + length + breadth = 2 x (length + breadth).
In a shape with all equal sides, perimeter is the number of sides x one side. For a square of 5 cm: 4 x 5 = 20 cm.
To choose the lace, find the perimeter first, then pick the lace of exactly that length or use two laces whose lengths add up to it.
Draw rectangles of perimeter 26 cm: length + breadth = 13, so 8 x 5 or 10 x 3 or 7 x 6. For 18 cm: length + breadth = 9, so 5 x 4 or 6 x 3 or 7 x 2.
Many rectangles can have the same perimeter, with different shapes.
To find the perimeter of any shape, add all its side lengths, or walk along the border.

problem.en: Find the perimeter of a rectangle 9 cm long and 4 cm broad.

why.en: Go around the shape adding each side.
Add length and breadth, double it.

prompt.en: How do you find the perimeter of a square quilt of side 5 units?

requiredIdeas.en: A square has four equal sides

points.en: Perimeter is the length of the border.
Rectangle: 2 x (l + b); square: 4 x side.
Different shapes can have the same perimeter.
